newsitem.title: USA: Boulder officials deny JonBenet probe stalled.
newsitem.headline: Boulder officials deny JonBenet probe stalled.

text.p: A Boulder official investigating the murder of 6-year old beauty pageant winner JonBenet Ramsey denied on Thursday the investigation had reached a standstill.

"I don't believe it's at a stalled state at all. A tremendous amount of work is going on ... It is a lot of re-interviewing," Boulder County District Attorney Alex Hunter told a weekly news briefing. "It is following up new leads that come in on a daily basis, some good, some bad ... I feel we're right on track."

Hunter also said investigators had interviewed Marilyn Van Derbur Atler, a Colorado native and former Miss America who disclosed in 1991 that she had been a victim of child abuse at the hands of her wealthy father.

Atler, who was Miss America in 1958 and did not make the revelations until after her prominent father died, has become an outspoken advocate for victims of child sexual abuse. Hunter, who went to school with Atler, called her a "significant resource to our investigation."
Boulder spokeswoman Leslie Aaholm told reporters: "We did have a good conversation with her."
No arrests have been made and no suspects named in the nine-week old murder probe. But Hunter said investigators had recently returned from a 10-day trip to five states.
He also said DNA material was expected to be sent to Maryland laboratory Cellmark next week and that it was unlikely an arrest would be made before the results were back.
"I like to think of myself as an evidence man," Hunter said.
No formal interviews have been conducted with JonBenet's parents, John and Patricia Ramsey. Hunter said negotiations were being conducted with the lawyers for the Ramseys.

He did not disclose which issues were preventing a face-to-face formal interview but Ramsey family spokesman Pat Korten has said the parents wanted to meet with police away from the police station to avoid publicity.

Police have not ruled anybody out as a suspect and Hunter said detectives were looking into the alibi of John Andrew Ramsey, JonBenet's older half-brother who attends college in Colorado. "We have more work to do on John Andrew's alibi," Hunter said, without elaborating.
Previously, the police said John Andrew Ramsey was believed to be out of town at the time of the murder.
The body of JonBenet was found on Dec. 26 by her father in the basement of the family's home, some eight hours after her mother said she found a ransom note demanding $118,000.
Hunter also said no decision had been made on whether to pursue the death penalty if a suspect were arrested. "It's way premature (to make that decision)," he said.
